metadata.title: ScriptSliderPack
metadata.description: Multi-slider array UI component for editing SliderPackData with step and drag workflows.

text: Table curve editor component with complex-data binding, drag customization, and external table linking.
body:
::category-tags
---
tags:
  - { name: ui, desc: "UI components, rendering, and visual tools" }
  - { name: component, desc: "Visual UI component on the script interface" }
---
::

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "ScriptTable (UI Reference)", to: "/v2/reference/ui-components/components/scripttable", desc: "CSS styling, properties reference, and visual customization" }
  - { label: "ScriptSliderPack", to: "/v2/scripting-api/scriptsliderpack", desc: "Use ScriptTable for smooth curve editing with draggable control points; use ScriptSliderPack for editing discrete step values in an array." }
  - { label: "ScriptAudioWaveform", to: "/v2/scripting-api/scriptaudiowaveform", desc: "Use ScriptTable for parameter curve editing; use ScriptAudioWaveform for displaying and interacting with audio sample data." }
  - { label: "Table", to: "/v2/scripting-api/table", desc: "ScriptTable is the UI component that displays and edits a Table data object" }
---
::



## Overview

`ScriptTable` is a curve editor component for shaping normalised values with draggable points.

Use it when you want a user-editable transfer curve for velocity mapping, modulation shaping, or other response remapping where a single x-to-y lookup drives runtime behaviour. You can either create it in script with `Content.addTable(...)` or bind to an existing designed component with `Content.getComponent(...)`, then configure drag rules and data binding during `onInit`.

```js
const var st = Content.addTable("EnvCurve", 20, 20);
const var existing = Content.getComponent("Table1");
```

Typical ScriptTable workflows are:

1. Build one curve and query it with `getTableValue()` from note or control callbacks.
2. Register the table once with `registerAtParent()` and reuse the returned data handle in runtime code.
3. Apply a shared local look-and-feel created with `Content.createLocalLookAndFeel()`, then attach it with `setLocalLookAndFeel()` to keep multiple tables visually consistent.

### Interaction

Hold Ctrl and scroll the mouse wheel over a line segment to adjust its curve. This works for all table editors in HISE, including envelope displays.

Dragging table points does not trigger the control callback (`onControl` or `setControlCallback`). To run callback logic after a user edits the curve, call `changed()` explicitly from script or use the table data directly via `getTableValue()`.

### Styling

Set the `customColours` property to `true` to switch to flat-style rendering. This enables the standard colour properties (`bgColour`, `itemColour`, etc.) for table styling. Without this flag, colour properties have no effect on the table appearance.

## Complex Data Chain

Table workflows use a three-part complex-data chain:

![Table Data Chain](/images/v2/scripting-api/topology_complex-table-data-chain.svg)

- `TableProcessor` selects the module that owns one or more table slots.
- `Table` is the complex-data handle for one slot within that module.
- `ScriptTable` displays or edits one selected slot in the UI.

Use the binding properties separately:

- `processorId` selects the owning processor.
- `tableIndex` selects which table slot inside that processor should be displayed.

This is not the normal parameter binding path. `parameterId` targets processor parameters, while table-slot binding uses `tableIndex` instead.

`setSnapValues()` configures x-axis snap points for point dragging, while `setMouseHandlingProperties()` controls edit behaviour such as edge locking, swap rules, and grid stepping.

::tip{title="Setup once in onInit, reuse handles"}
ScriptTable is a UI component. Do setup work once in `onInit` and reuse handles at runtime. Also note that `addToMacroControl()` is intentionally not active for ScriptTable, and `setPropertiesFromJSON()` should be done via `Content.setPropertiesFromJSON(componentId, jsonData)`.
::

::common-mistakes
---
mistakes:
  - title: "Normalise input to 0-1 range"
    wrong: "`table.getTableValue(Message.getVelocity())`"
    right: "`table.getTableValue(Message.getVelocity() / 127.0)`"
    reason: "Table lookup input is normalised. Raw MIDI values collapse the curve response."
  - title: "Register at parent once at init time"
    wrong: "Calling `registerAtParent()` inside `onNoteOn`"
    right: "Call `registerAtParent()` once in `onInit` and cache the returned handle"
    reason: "Registration is setup work, not per-note work. Repeating it during playback adds avoidable overhead."
  - title: "setSnapValues takes an array"
    wrong: "`st.setSnapValues(0.25)`"
    right: "`st.setSnapValues([0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0])`"
    reason: "Snap values must be an array of x positions."
  - title: "referToData requires same data type"
    wrong: "`st.referToData(sliderPackDataObj)`"
    right: "`st.referToData(tableDataObj)`"
    reason: "`referToData` only accepts table-compatible data sources."
  - title: "Override all table draw functions together"
    wrong: "Styling only one table draw function"
    right: "Override the full set (`drawTableBackground`, `drawTablePath`, `drawTablePoint`, `drawTableRuler`)"
    reason: "Partial overrides often produce mixed default/custom rendering that looks inconsistent."
---
::
## Usage Example

```javascript
const var st = Content.addTable("EnvCurve", 20, 20);
st.setTablePoint(1, 0.5, 0.8, 0.5);
st.setMouseHandlingProperties({ "allowSwap": false, "numSteps": 8 });
```

## Methods

::method-heading
---
name: addTablePoint
params:
  - { name: x, type: double, desc: "Normalized x position for the new point" }
  - { name: y, type: double, desc: "Normalized y value for the new point" }
---
::

```javascript
st.addTablePoint(0.5, 0.75);
```


Adds a new point to the table curve at the given normalised x/y position. Use this when building a curve procedurally instead of editing existing point indices.

::warning{title="Values not clamped to 0-1 range"}
Values are not clamped automatically, so keep x and y in the 0.0 to 1.0 range to avoid unexpected curve shapes.
::

::see-also
---
links:

  - { label: "reset", to: "#reset" }
---
::

::method-heading

name: addToMacroControl
params:
  - { name: macroIndex, type: int, desc: "" }
---
::

This method is not active for ScriptTable. Table components intentionally do not participate in macro control assignment.

Use curve lookup or data-sharing workflows (`getTableValue()`, `registerAtParent()`) instead of macro mapping.

---

::method-heading{name="changed"}
::
Triggers the table component's control callback manually. Use it when you update related state in script and want callback-driven logic to run.

::warning{title="Ignored during onInit"}
Calls made during `onInit` are ignored.
::

Toggles visibility with a fade animation over the specified duration in milliseconds. Only triggers if the target visibility state differs from the current state. For instant visibility changes without animation, use `showControl()`.

::method-heading

params:
  - { name: propertyName, type: String, desc: "" }
---
::

Returns the value of a component property. See `set()` for the full property list.

---

::method-heading{name="getAllProperties"}
::
Returns an array of all active property IDs for this component. ScriptTable hides the usual scalar-range and parameter-link properties because it binds to table data rather than a single numeric value.

---

::method-heading{name="getChildComponents"}
::
Returns an array of references to all child components whose `parentComponent` property is set to this component.

---

::method-heading{name="getGlobalPositionX"}
::
Returns the absolute x-position of this component relative to the interface root, accounting for all parent component offsets.

---

::method-heading{name="getGlobalPositionY"}
::
Returns the absolute y-position of this component relative to the interface root, accounting for all parent component offsets.

---

::method-heading{name="getHeight"}
::
Returns the height of this component in pixels.

---

::method-heading{name="getId"}
::
Returns the component's ID as a string.

::method-heading
---
name: getLocalBounds
params:
  - { name: reduceAmount, type: double, desc: "" }
---
::

Returns a `[x, y, w, h]` array representing the component's local bounds, inset by the given pixel amount from each edge. Pass `0` to get the full bounds `[0, 0, width, height]`.

---

::method-heading
---
name: getTableValue
params:
  - { name: inputValue, type: double, desc: "Normalized lookup position" }
---
::

```javascript
var y = st.getTableValue(0.25);
```


Looks up the curve output for a normalised input position and returns the interpolated value. This is the main runtime read path for velocity and modulation transfer functions.

::warning{title="Normalise input to 0-1 range"}
Input must be normalised to 0.0 to 1.0. Passing raw MIDI values makes the mapping behave almost constant.
::

#### Velocity Curve Transfer Function (validated)

```javascript
// Context: A MIDI script shapes incoming velocity with a user-editable curve.

const var velocityCurve = Content.addTable("VelocityCurve", 10, 10);
velocityCurve.set("width", 240);
velocityCurve.set("height", 100);
velocityCurve.addTablePoint(0.5, 0.25);

inline function applyVelocityCurve(inputVelocity)
{
    local normalized = inputVelocity / 127.0;
    local mapped = velocityCurve.getTableValue(normalized);
    return Math.max(1, Math.round(mapped * 127.0));
}

function onNoteOn()
{
    Message.setVelocity(applyVelocityCurve(Message.getVelocity()));
}
```

::see-also

links:

  - { label: "registerAtParent", to: "#registeratparent" }
  - { label: "ScriptTableData.getTableValueNormalised", to: "/v2/scripting-api/scripttabledata#gettablevaluenormalised" }

st.referToData(otherTable);

Rebinds this table editor to another table data source. Pass a table data handle, a compatible table component, or `-1` to switch back to this component's internal table.

#### Script Table Refer To Data (skipped)

```javascript
const var TableA = Content.addTable("TableA", 0, 0);
const var TableB = Content.addTable("TableB", 0, 80);

const var sharedData = TableA.registerAtParent(0);
TableB.referToData(sharedData);
```

::method-heading

name: registerAtParent
params:
  - { name: index, type: int, desc: "External table slot index at the parent processor" }
---
::

```javascript
var td = st.registerAtParent(0);
```


Registers this table's owned data in a parent processor slot and returns a handle you can reuse outside the UI layer. This is the standard bridge when playback callbacks need the same curve shown in the editor.

::warning{title="Register once and cache the handle"}
Register once during setup and cache the handle. Re-registering in note or control callbacks adds avoidable runtime overhead.
::

#### Register Table For Runtime Lookup (skipped)

```javascript
// Context: The table editor stays in the UI layer, while note callbacks read a shared data handle.

const var velocityTable = Content.addTable("VelocityTable", 10, 10);
velocityTable.set("width", 280);
velocityTable.set("height", 120);

const var velocityData = velocityTable.registerAtParent(0);

inline function mapVelocity(rawVelocity)
{
    local normalized = rawVelocity / 127.0;
    local shaped = velocityData.getTableValueNormalised(normalized) * 127.0;
    return Math.range(Math.round(shaped), 1, 127);
}

function onNoteOn()
{
    Message.setVelocity(mapVelocity(Message.getVelocity()));
}
```

::see-also

links:
  - { label: "referToData", to: "#refertodata" }

::method-heading{name="reset"}
::

```javascript
st.reset();
```

Resets the table to its default linear shape from `(0, 0)` to `(1, 1)`. This call takes no index and resets the entire curve.

::see-also

links:
  - { label: "addTablePoint", to: "#addtablepoint" }

::method-heading{name="sendRepaintMessage"}
::
Queues an asynchronous repaint of this component. Call this after changing visual properties programmatically when the component does not repaint automatically.

---

::method-heading
---
name: set
params:
  - { name: propertyName, type: String, desc: "" }
  - { name: value, type: var, desc: "" }
---
::

Sets a component property to the given value. During `onInit`, changes are applied without UI notification; outside `onInit`, the UI updates automatically.

| Property | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `x`, `y`, `width`, `height` | Position and size in pixels, relative to parent |
| `visible`, `enabled`, `locked` | Display and interaction state |
| `text`, `tooltip` | Display text and hover tooltip |
| `bgColour`, `itemColour`, `itemColour2`, *`customColours`* | Colour properties and custom colour rendering |
| `parentComponent` | Parent component for layout nesting |
| `saveInPreset`, `useUndoManager`, `deferControlCallback` | Preset persistence, undo, and callback deferral |
| `processorId`, *`tableIndex`* | Complex data source: the connected processor and the table slot to use from that processor or external data holder |

---

::method-heading
---
name: setConsumedKeyPresses
params:
  - { name: listOfKeys, type: var, desc: "" }
---
::

Defines which key presses this component captures when it has focus. Pass `"all"` to consume all keys exclusively, `"all_nonexclusive"` to receive all keys while still letting the parent handle them, or an array of key descriptions (strings like `"ctrl + S"` or objects with `keyCode`, `shift`, `cmd`, `alt` properties).

| Value | Behaviour |
|-------|-----------|
| `"all"` | Catches all keys exclusively - parent does not receive them |
| `"all_nonexclusive"` | Catches all keys but parent still receives them |
| Array of strings/objects | Catches only the specified key combinations |

::warning{title="Call before setKeyPressCallback"}
Must be called before `setKeyPressCallback()`. Calling them in the wrong order reports a script error.
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: setControlCallback
params:
  - { name: controlFunction, type: var, desc: "" }
---
::

Assigns a custom inline function as the control callback for this component, replacing the default `onControl` handler. The function receives two parameters: the component reference and the new value. Pass `false` to revert to the default `onControl` callback.

::warning{title="Requires inline function with two parameters"}
The function must be declared with `inline function` and must have exactly two parameters. Regular function references are rejected with a script error.
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: setKeyPressCallback
params:
  - { name: keyboardFunction, type: var, desc: "" }
---
::

Registers a callback that fires when a consumed key is pressed while this component has focus. The callback receives an event object describing the key press or a focus change event.

For key press events, the object contains `isFocusChange` (false), `character`, `specialKey`, `keyCode`, `description`, and modifier flags (`shift`, `cmd`, `alt`). For focus change events, it contains `isFocusChange` (true) and `hasFocus`.

::warning{title="Call setConsumedKeyPresses first"}
You must call `setConsumedKeyPresses()` before this method. Calling them in the wrong order reports a script error.
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: setLocalLookAndFeel
params:
  - { name: lafObject, type: var, desc: "" }
---
::

Attaches a scripted look and feel object to this component and all its children. Pass `false` to clear it. The relevant LAF functions are `drawTableBackground`, `drawTablePath`, `drawTablePoint`, `drawTableMidPoint`, and `drawTableRuler`.

#### Shared Table Laf (skipped)

```javascript
// Context: A modulation page applies one table-specific LAF to all curve editors.

const var tableA = Content.addTable("TableA", 10, 10);
const var tableB = Content.addTable("TableB", 10, 130);

const var tableLaf = Content.createLocalLookAndFeel();

tableLaf.registerFunction("drawTableBackground", function(g, obj)
{
    g.setColour(0xFF202225);
    g.fillRoundedRectangle(obj.area, 4.0);
});

tableLaf.registerFunction("drawTablePath", function(g, obj)
{
    g.setGradientFill([obj.itemColour, 0.0, 0.0, obj.itemColour2, 0.0, obj.area[3], false]);
    g.drawPath(obj.path, Rectangle(obj.area), 1.5);
});

tableLaf.registerFunction("drawTablePoint", function(g, obj)
{
    g.setColour(obj.hover ? Colours.white : 0xAAFFFFFF);
    g.fillEllipse(Rectangle(obj.tablePoint).reduced(2));
});

tableLaf.registerFunction("drawTableRuler", function(g, obj)
{
    g.setColour(0x88FFFFFF);
    g.fillRect([obj.position * obj.area[2], 0, 2, obj.area[3]]);
});

tableA.setLocalLookAndFeel(tableLaf);
tableB.setLocalLookAndFeel(tableLaf);
```

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "ScriptLookAndFeel.registerFunction", to: "/v2/scripting-api/scriptlookandfeel#registerfunction" }
---
::

::method-heading

name: setMouseHandlingProperties
params:
  - { name: propertyObject, type: var, desc: "Mouse-drag configuration object" }
---
::

```javascript
st.setMouseHandlingProperties({"allowSwap": true, "snapWidth": 8.0});
```


Configures table drag behaviour from a JSON object, including edge locks, point swap rules, step grids, and curve edit options. Use this to define editing ergonomics for your table UI.

#### Script Table Mouse Drag Properties (skipped)

```javascript
const var Table1 = Content.addTable("Table1", 0, 0);

Table1.setMouseHandlingProperties({
    "allowSwap": false,
    "syncStartEnd": true,
    "numSteps": 8,
    "snapWidth": 6.0,
    "fixLeftEdge": 0.0,
    "fixRightEdge": 1.0
});
```

::see-also

links:
  - { label: "setSnapValues", to: "#setsnapvalues" }
  - { label: "setTablePoint", to: "#settablepoint" }
  - { label: "setTablePopupFunction", to: "#settablepopupfunction" }

::

::method-heading

name: setPosition
params:
  - { name: x, type: int, desc: "" }

  - { name: w, type: int, desc: "" }
  - { name: h, type: int, desc: "" }

::

Sets the position and size of this component in one call. Coordinates are in pixels, relative to the parent component.

::method-heading

params:
  - { name: jsonData, type: var, desc: "" }

::

This method is not exposed directly on ScriptTable instances in this API path. To restore component properties from JSON, use `Content.setPropertiesFromJSON(componentId, jsonData)`.

::method-heading

name: setSnapValues
params:
  - { name: snapValueArray, type: Array, desc: "Normalized snap x positions" }
---
::

```javascript
st.setSnapValues([0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0]);
```


Sets x-axis snap targets used while dragging table points. Pass an array of normalised positions such as `[0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0]`.

This configures point snapping only and does not bind the table to any processor.

::see-also

  - { label: "setTablePopupFunction", to: "#settablepopupfunction" }

::method-heading

name: setStyleSheetClass
params:
  - { name: classIds, type: String, desc: "" }
---
::

Sets CSS class selectors on this component for stylesheet-based styling. The component's type class (`.scripttable`) is automatically prepended, so passing `".primary"` results in the selector `.scripttable .primary`. Use `setStyleSheetProperty()` instead when you only need to change a single CSS variable rather than switching the entire class.

---

::method-heading
---
name: setStyleSheetProperty
params:
  - { name: variableId, type: String, desc: "" }
  - { name: value, type: var, desc: "" }
  - { name: type, type: String, desc: "" }
---
::

Sets a CSS variable on this component that can be referenced from a stylesheet. The `type` parameter controls how the value is converted to a CSS-compatible string.

| Type | Conversion |
|------|-----------|
| `"color"` | Integer colour to `#AARRGGBB` string |
| `"%"` | Number to percentage (0.5 becomes `"50%"`) |
| `"px"` | Number to pixel value |
| `"em"` | Number to em value |
| `"vh"` | Number to viewport-height value |
| `"deg"` | Number to degree value |
| `"path"` | Path object to base64-encoded string |
| `""` | No conversion - stored as-is |

---

::method-heading
---
name: setStyleSheetPseudoState
params:
  - { name: pseudoState, type: String, desc: "" }
---
::

Sets CSS pseudo-state selectors on this component for stylesheet-based styling. Multiple states can be combined in a single string (e.g. `":hover:active"`). Pass an empty string to clear all pseudo-states. The component automatically repaints after the state changes.

| Pseudo-state | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `:hover` | Mouse hover |
| `:active` | Active/pressed |
| `:focus` | Keyboard focus |
| `:checked` | Toggled/checked |
| `:disabled` | Disabled |
| `:hidden` | Hidden |
| `:first-child` | First child |
| `:last-child` | Last child |
| `:root` | Root element |

---

::method-heading
---
name: setTablePoint
params:
  - { name: pointIndex, type: int, desc: "Graph point index to edit" }
  - { name: x, type: double, desc: "New normalized x value" }
  - { name: y, type: double, desc: "New normalized y value" }
  - { name: curve, type: double, desc: "Curve amount toward next point" }
---
::

```javascript
st.setTablePoint(1, 0.5, 0.8, 0.5);
```


Updates an existing table point by index, including x position, y value, and curve amount toward the next point.

::warning{title="Edge point x positions are fixed"}
The first and last points keep fixed x positions at `0` and `1`, even if you pass different x values.
::

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "addTablePoint", to: "#addtablepoint" }
  - { label: "getTableValue", to: "#gettablevalue" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: setTablePopupFunction
params:
  - { name: newFunction, type: Function, desc: "Popup text formatter callback, or `false` to fall back to default popup text" }
---
::

```javascript
st.setTablePopupFunction(onTablePopupText);
```


Sets a formatter callback for the point-drag popup text. The callback receives normalised `x` and `y` values and returns the string to display.

::warning{title="Null or empty hides popup text"}
Returning `null` or an empty string hides popup text. Call `setTablePopupFunction(false)` to restore the default popup formatter.
::

#### Toggle Table Popup Verbosity (skipped)

```javascript
// Context: Dense editors often hide drag popup text to keep nearby controls visible.

const var lfoTable = Content.addTable("LfoTable", 10, 10);
const var compactMode = Content.addButton("CompactMode", 10, 130);

inline function formatPopup(x, y)
{
    return parseInt(x * 100) + "% | " + parseInt(y * 100) + "%";
}

inline function hidePopup(x, y)
{
    return "";
}

lfoTable.setTablePopupFunction(formatPopup);

inline function onCompactModeControl(component, value)
{
    if (value)
        lfoTable.setTablePopupFunction(hidePopup);
    else
        lfoTable.setTablePopupFunction(false);
}

compactMode.setControlCallback(onCompactModeControl);
```

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "setMouseHandlingProperties", to: "#setmousehandlingproperties" }
  - { label: "setSnapValues", to: "#setsnapvalues" }
  - { label: "setMouseHandlingProperties", to: "#setmousehandlingproperties" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: setTooltip
params:
  - { name: tooltip, type: String, desc: "" }
---
::

Sets the tooltip text displayed when the mouse hovers over this component.

---

::method-heading
---
name: setValue
params:
  - { name: newValue, type: var, desc: "" }
---
::

Sets the base component value for this ScriptTable. Use this for generic component state flows rather than curve point editing.

::warning{title="Values not restored after recompile"}
Values assigned during `onInit` are not restored automatically after recompilation.
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: setValueNormalized
params:
  - { name: normalizedValue, type: double, desc: "" }
---
::

Sets the base component value using a 0.0 to 1.0 normalised input.

---

::method-heading
---
name: setValueWithUndo
params:
  - { name: newValue, type: var, desc: "" }
---
::

Sets the value through the undo manager, allowing the change to be reverted. Use this for user-initiated value changes that should support undo/redo.

::warning{title="Avoid calling from control callbacks"}
Do not call this from `onControl` or a custom control callback. The undo operation itself triggers the control callback, creating a feedback loop.
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: setZLevel
params:
  - { name: zLevel, type: String, desc: "" }
---
::

Sets the depth level for this component among its siblings. The value must be one of four case-sensitive strings:

| Value | Behaviour |
|-------|-----------|
| `"Back"` | Renders behind all siblings |
| `"Default"` | Normal rendering order |
| `"Front"` | Renders in front of normal siblings |
| `"AlwaysOnTop"` | Always renders on top of all siblings |

---

::method-heading
---
name: showControl
params:
  - { name: shouldBeVisible, type: bool, desc: "" }
---
::

Shows or hides this component immediately. Pass `1` to show, `0` to hide. For an animated transition, use `fadeComponent()` instead.

---

::method-heading{name="updateValueFromProcessorConnection"}
::
Reads the current value from the connected processor (set via the `processorId` and `parameterId` properties) and updates this component accordingly. Does nothing if no processor connection is established.

---

text: Script handle to a module with SliderPack data, providing indexed data references.
body:
## Overview

SliderPackProcessor is a lightweight wrapper around any audio module that contains SliderPack data - step sequencers, array modulators, harmonic filters, and similar modules with indexed slider arrays. Obtained via `Synth.getSliderPackProcessor()`, it provides access to the module's SliderPack data objects by index.

```js
const var spp = Synth.getSliderPackProcessor("ArrayModulator1");
const var pack = spp.getSliderPack(0);
```

The returned `SliderPackData` reference lets you read and write individual slider values, resize the pack, and perform other slider pack operations. This follows the same processor-wrapper pattern as `TableProcessor` for table data and `AudioSampleProcessor` for audio file data.

## Complex Data Chain

Slider-pack workflows use a three-part complex-data chain:

![Slider Pack Data Chain](/images/v2/scripting-api/topology_complex-sliderpack-data-chain.svg)

- `SliderPackProcessor` selects the module that owns one or more slider-pack slots.
- `SliderPackData` is the complex-data handle for one slot within that module.
- `ScriptSliderPack` displays or edits one selected slot in the UI.

Use the binding properties separately:

- `processorId` selects the owning processor.
- `SliderPackIndex` selects which slider-pack slot inside that processor should be displayed.

This is not the normal parameter binding path. `parameterId` targets processor parameters, while slider-pack binding uses `SliderPackIndex` instead.

::tip{title="Accepts any module with SliderPack data"}
The wrapper accepts any module that holds SliderPack data internally, not only modules whose name suggests slider pack functionality.
::

::common-mistakes
---
mistakes:
  - title: "Cache processor reference in onInit"
    wrong: "`var spp = Synth.getSliderPackProcessor(\"MyModule\");` called in `onNoteOn`"
    right: "`const var spp = Synth.getSliderPackProcessor(\"MyModule\");` in `onInit`"
    reason: "The factory method requires the object creation phase and will throw an error if called inside a callback."
---
::
## Usage Example

```javascript
// Get a reference to a module's slider pack data
const var spp = Synth.getSliderPackProcessor("ArrayModulator1");
const var pack = spp.getSliderPack(0);
```

## Methods

::method-heading
---
name: getSliderPack
params:
  - { name: sliderPackIndex, type: int, desc: "Zero-based index of the slider pack slot to access" }
---
::

```javascript
var sp = spp.getSliderPack(0);
```


Returns a `SliderPackData` reference for the slider pack at the given index. The index is zero-based and refers to the slider pack slots owned by the target module - index 0 for a single-pack module like an array modulator, or indices 0-2 for a module with three packs like a harmonic filter.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "Synth.getSliderPackProcessor", to: "/v2/scripting-api/synth#getsliderpackprocessor" }
  - { label: "API.ScriptSliderPackData$` -- the returned data handle class (HiseScript name: SliderPackData)", to: "/v2/scripting-api/api#scriptsliderpackdata$` -- the returned data handle class (hisescript name: sliderpackdata)" }
  - { label: "TableProcessor.getTable", to: "/v2/scripting-api/tableprocessor#gettable" }
  - { label: "AudioSampleProcessor.getAudioFile", to: "/v2/scripting-api/audiosampleprocessor#getaudiofile" }
---
::

---

text: Multi-dimensional bitmask-based sample group controller for advanced layer, crossfade, and articulation management.
body:
::category-tags
---
tags:
  - { name: module-tree, desc: "Audio engine, module tree navigation, and processor handles" }
  - { name: handle, desc: "Script handle to a module or resource managed elsewhere" }
---
::

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "Sampler", to: "/v2/scripting-api/sampler", desc: "ComplexGroupManager provides fine-grained per-layer/per-group voice control (fades, delays, volumes), while Sampler handles sample map loading and basic RR group switching." }
---
::



## Overview

ComplexGroupManager provides multi-dimensional control over sample group filtering for a Sampler. Instead of the Sampler's single round-robin group index, it organises samples into independent layers, each with its own filtering logic. A 64-bit bitmask encodes every sample's membership across all layers, so multiple dimensions can be evaluated simultaneously during voice start.

```js
const var cgm = Sampler1.getComplexGroupManager();
```

Each layer has a LogicType that determines its automatic behaviour:

| LogicType | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| Custom | Scriptable layer with per-group volume and voice start callbacks |
| RoundRobin | Automatic round-robin cycling on each note |
| Keyswitch | MIDI-key-driven articulation switching |
| TableFade | Legacy crossfade using the Sampler's crossfade tables |
| XFade | Dynamic crossfade from EventData, MIDI CC, or GlobalMod sources |
| LegatoInterval | Phase-locked legato transition samples |
| ReleaseTrigger | Automatic release sample triggering with gain matching |
| Choke | Mutual voice cancellation between groups |

Layers are configured through string property IDs via `getLayerProperty()` and `setLayerProperty()`. Voice start parameters (delay, fade-in, start offset, fixed length) are set per layer/group before a noteOn and consumed when voices start.

The constant `ComplexGroupManager.IgnoreFlag` (255) indicates that a layer does not apply to a given sample. Methods that accept a layer identifier take either a zero-based numeric index or a string layer ID.

::tip{title="Zero-based group indices, next-noteOn configuration"}
All group indices in the scripting API are zero-based. The internal bitmask is one-based, but the conversion is automatic. Methods that modify voice start parameters (`delayGroupEvent`, `fadeInGroupEvent`, `addGroupEventStartOffset`, `setFixedGroupEventLength`) configure data for the next noteOn - they do not affect already-playing voices.
::

::common-mistakes
---
mistakes:
  - title: "setGroupVolume requires Custom LogicType"
    wrong: "`cgm.setGroupVolume(0, 1, 0.5);` on a non-Custom layer"
    right: "`cgm.setGroupVolume(0, 1, 0.5);` on a Custom layer"
    reason: "`setGroupVolume` only works with Custom LogicType layers. On other layer types, the call silently does nothing."
  - title: "Call createNoteMap before querying"
    wrong: "`cgm.isNoteNumberMapped(0, 60);` without calling `createNoteMap` first"
    right: "`cgm.createNoteMap(0); cgm.isNoteNumberMapped(0, 60);`"
    reason: "`isNoteNumberMapped` requires `createNoteMap()` to have been called first for the same layer. Call it again after loading a new sample map."
  - title: "Enable gain tracking before reading peaks"
    wrong: "`cgm.getCurrentPeak(0, 1, eventId);` without enabling tracking"
    right: "`cgm.setEnableGainTracking(0, 1, true);` then later `cgm.getCurrentPeak(0, 1, eventId);`"
    reason: "Peak tracking must be explicitly enabled per layer/group pair before values can be read."
---
::
## Usage Example

```javascript
// Get the ComplexGroupManager from a Sampler
const var cgm = Sampler.getComplexGroupManager();

// Query layer structure
const var numGroups = cgm.getNumGroupsInLayer(0);

// Set the active group for the first layer
cgm.setActiveGroup(0, 0);
```

## Methods

::method-heading
---
name: addGroupEventStartOffset
params:
  - { name: layerIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based layer index" }
  - { name: groupIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based group index within the layer" }
  - { name: offsetSamples, type: double, desc: "Sample start offset in samples" }
---
::

```javascript
cgm.addGroupEventStartOffset(0, 1, 4096);
```


Sets the sample start offset for voices matching a layer/group combination on the next noteOn. Playback begins from the specified sample position instead of the sample's default start point.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "delayGroupEvent", to: "#delaygroupevent" }
  - { label: "fadeInGroupEvent", to: "#fadeingroupevent" }
  - { label: "setFixedGroupEventLength", to: "#setfixedgroupeventlength" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: createNoteMap
params:
  - { name: layerIdOrIndex, type: double, desc: "Layer index or string layer ID" }
---
::

```javascript
cgm.createNoteMap(0);
```


Builds a note-to-group lookup table for the specified layer by scanning all samples in the current sample map. The resulting map is used by `isNoteNumberMapped()` for fast per-note queries. Call this again after loading a new sample map to keep the lookup current.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "isNoteNumberMapped", to: "#isnotenumbermapped" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: delayGroupEvent
params:
  - { name: layerIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based layer index" }
  - { name: groupIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based group index within the layer" }
  - { name: delayInSamples, type: double, desc: "Delay time in samples" }
---
::

```javascript
cgm.delayGroupEvent(0, 1, 4410.0);
```


Delays the voice start for a layer/group combination on the next noteOn by the specified number of samples. Use this together with `addGroupEventStartOffset()` and `fadeInGroupEvent()` to stagger or shape how layered voices enter.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "addGroupEventStartOffset", to: "#addgroupeventstartoffset" }
  - { label: "fadeInGroupEvent", to: "#fadeingroupevent" }
  - { label: "setFixedGroupEventLength", to: "#setfixedgroupeventlength" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: fadeInGroupEvent
params:
  - { name: layerIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based layer index" }
  - { name: groupIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based group index within the layer" }
  - { name: fadeInTimeMs, type: double, desc: "Fade-in duration in milliseconds" }
  - { name: targetGainDb, type: double, desc: "Target gain in decibels" }
---
::

```javascript
cgm.fadeInGroupEvent(0, 1, 100.0, 0.0);
```


Sets a fade-in duration (in milliseconds) and target gain (in decibels) for voices matching a layer/group combination on the next noteOn. A target gain of 0.0 dB means unity gain; use negative values for attenuation.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "fadeOutGroupEvent", to: "#fadeoutgroupevent" }
  - { label: "delayGroupEvent", to: "#delaygroupevent" }
  - { label: "addGroupEventStartOffset", to: "#addgroupeventstartoffset" }
  - { label: "setFixedGroupEventLength", to: "#setfixedgroupeventlength" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: fadeOutGroupEvent
params:
  - { name: layerIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based layer index" }
  - { name: groupIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based group index within the layer" }
  - { name: fadeOutTimeMs, type: double, desc: "Fade-out duration in milliseconds" }
---
::

```javascript
cgm.fadeOutGroupEvent(0, 1, 200.0);
```


Fades out all currently playing voices that match the specified layer/group combination over the given duration in milliseconds.

::warning{title="Only affects already-playing voices"}
Unlike `delayGroupEvent`, `fadeInGroupEvent`, and the other voice start methods, `fadeOutGroupEvent` acts on already-playing voices. Calling it before any matching voices are sounding has no effect.
::

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "fadeInGroupEvent", to: "#fadeingroupevent" }
  - { label: "setGroupVolume", to: "#setgroupvolume" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: getCurrentPeak
params:
  - { name: layerIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based layer index" }
  - { name: groupIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based group index within the layer" }
  - { name: eventId, type: double, desc: "Event ID of the voice to query" }
---
::

```javascript
var peak = cgm.getCurrentPeak(0, 1, Message.getEventId());
```


Returns the current peak volume of the voice matching the specified layer, group, and event ID. Gain tracking must be enabled first with `setEnableGainTracking()` for the same layer/group pair.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "setEnableGainTracking", to: "#setenablegaintracking" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: getLayerIndex
params:
  - { name: layerIdOrIndex, type: double, desc: "Layer index or string layer ID" }
---
::

```javascript
var idx = cgm.getLayerIndex("Articulation");
```


Resolves a string layer ID to its zero-based numeric index. If a number is passed, it is returned as-is. Useful when you store layer references by name but need the numeric index for other API calls.

---

::method-heading
---
name: getLayerProperty
params:
  - { name: layerIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based layer index" }
  - { name: propertyId, type: String, desc: "Property identifier" }
---
::

```javascript
var type = cgm.getLayerProperty(0, "type");
```


Returns the value of a layer configuration property. The return type depends on the property - most return a String or Number, but `tokens` returns a String array and `matrixString` returns an integer array.

| Property | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `"type"` | LogicType name (`"Custom"`, `"RR"`, `"Keyswitch"`, `"TableFade"`, `"XFade"`, `"Legato"`, `"Release"`, `"Choke"`) |
| `"id"` | Layer identifier string |
| `"tokens"` | Group names within the layer (String array) |
| `"colour"` | Display colour |
| `"folded"` | UI folded/collapsed state |
| `"ignorable"` | Whether samples in this layer can use IgnoreFlag |
| `"cached"` | Whether samples are pre-filtered into per-group containers |
| `"purgable"` | Whether samples can be purged by group value |
| `"fader"` | XFade curve type (`"Linear"`, `"RMS"`, `"Cosine half"`, `"Overlap"`, `"Switch"`) |
| `"slotIndex"` | XFade data slot index or MIDI CC number |
| `"sourceType"` | XFade input source (`"Event Data"`, `"Midi CC"`, `"GlobalMod"`) |
| `"matrixString"` | Choke group relationship matrix (integer array) |
| `"isChromatic"` | Whether keyswitch layer includes black keys |
| `"matchGain"` | Whether release layer matches sustain peak on release |
| `"accuracy"` | Release gain matching accuracy (0.0-1.0) |
| `"fadeTime"` | Fade duration in milliseconds |

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "setLayerProperty", to: "#setlayerproperty" }
  - { label: "getLayerIndex", to: "#getlayerindex" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: getNumGroupsInLayer
params:
  - { name: layerIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based layer index" }
---
::

```javascript
var num = cgm.getNumGroupsInLayer(0);
```


Returns the number of groups (tokens) defined in the specified layer. Use this to determine valid group index ranges before calling methods like `setActiveGroup()`.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "getLayerProperty", to: "#getlayerproperty" }
  - { label: "setActiveGroup", to: "#setactivegroup" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: isNoteNumberMapped
params:
  - { name: layerIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based layer index" }
  - { name: noteNumber, type: double, desc: "MIDI note number to check" }
---
::

```javascript
var mapped = cgm.isNoteNumberMapped(0, 60);
```


Returns 1 if any sample in the specified layer covers the given MIDI note number, 0 otherwise. Requires `createNoteMap()` to have been called first for the same layer.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "createNoteMap", to: "#createnotemap" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: registerGroupStartCallback
params:
  - { name: layerIdOrIndex, type: double, desc: "Layer index or string layer ID" }
  - { name: callback, type: Function, desc: "Realtime-safe callback for voice start events" }
---
::

```javascript
cgm.registerGroupStartCallback(0, onGroupStart);
```


Registers an inline function that is called when a voice starts for the specified layer. The callback receives the zero-based group index as its argument, which you can use to react to which group was triggered.

::warning{title="Handle IgnoreFlag value explicitly"}
The callback receives `ComplexGroupManager.IgnoreFlag` (255) as the group index when the started sample has no assignment in this layer. Handle this value explicitly rather than treating it as a regular group index.
::

#### Group Start Callback

```javascript
const var Sampler1 = Synth.getChildSynth("Sampler1");
const var cgm = Sampler1.getComplexGroupManager();

reg lastStartedGroup = -1;

inline function onGroupStart(groupIndex)
{
    if (groupIndex != cgm.IgnoreFlag)
        lastStartedGroup = groupIndex;
}

cgm.registerGroupStartCallback(0, onGroupStart);
```

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "setActiveGroup", to: "#setactivegroup" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: setActiveGroup
params:
  - { name: layerIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based layer index" }
  - { name: groupIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based group index to activate" }
---
::

```javascript
cgm.setActiveGroup(0, 2);
```


Sets the active group filter for a layer. On the next noteOn, only samples matching this group value in the given layer will be considered for voice start. The group index is zero-based.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "getNumGroupsInLayer", to: "#getnumgroupsinlayer" }
  - { label: "registerGroupStartCallback", to: "#registergroupstartcallback" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: setEnableGainTracking
params:
  - { name: layerIdOrIndex, type: double, desc: "Layer index or string layer ID" }
  - { name: groupIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based group index within the layer" }
  - { name: shouldBeActive, type: int, desc: "Enable (1) or disable (0) gain tracking" }
---
::

```javascript
cgm.setEnableGainTracking(0, 1, 1);
```


Enables or disables peak volume tracking for a specific layer/group combination. Once enabled, use `getCurrentPeak()` to read the tracked peak value for individual voices by event ID. This is typically used for release trigger gain matching in custom implementations.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "getCurrentPeak", to: "#getcurrentpeak" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: setFixedGroupEventLength
params:
  - { name: layerIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based layer index" }
  - { name: groupIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based group index within the layer" }
  - { name: numSamplesToPlayBeforeFadeout, type: double, desc: "Fixed playback length in samples before fadeout" }
---
::

```javascript
cgm.setFixedGroupEventLength(0, 1, 44100.0);
```


Sets a fixed playback length in samples for voices matching a layer/group combination on the next noteOn. Voices are automatically faded out after the specified number of samples, regardless of when the note-off arrives.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "delayGroupEvent", to: "#delaygroupevent" }
  - { label: "fadeInGroupEvent", to: "#fadeingroupevent" }
  - { label: "addGroupEventStartOffset", to: "#addgroupeventstartoffset" }
---
::

::method-heading
---
name: setGroupVolume
params:
  - { name: layerIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based layer index" }
  - { name: groupIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based group index within the layer" }
  - { name: gainFactor, type: double, desc: "Linear gain multiplier" }
---
::

```javascript
cgm.setGroupVolume(0, 1, 0.5);
```


Sets the linear gain multiplier for a specific layer/group combination. A value of 1.0 is unity gain; 0.0 is silence.

::warning{title="Only works with Custom LogicType layers"}
Only works with Custom LogicType layers. On other layer types, the call silently does nothing without producing an error message.
::

::see-also

params:
  - { name: layerIndex, type: double, desc: "Zero-based layer index" }

```javascript
cgm.setLayerProperty(0, "fadeTime", 50.0);
```


Sets a layer configuration property value. For `tokens`, pass a String array (stored internally as comma-separated text). For `matrixString`, pass an integer array. Changes to structural properties like `tokens` trigger a full layer and bitmask rebuild.

See `getLayerProperty()` for the complete list of property IDs and their types.

text: Scriptnode connection handle linking a source node or macro parameter to a target parameter.
body:
::category-tags
---
tags:
  - { name: scriptnode, desc: "ScriptNode DSP graph system" }
  - { name: handle, desc: "Script handle to a module or resource managed elsewhere" }
---
::

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "Parameter", to: "/v2/scripting-api/parameter", desc: "Connection is the link object that routes a signal to a Parameter; Parameter is the endpoint that receives the value." }
  - { label: "Node", to: "/v2/scripting-api/node", desc: "Connection represents the wiring between nodes; Node is the processing unit that produces or consumes the signal." }
---
::



## Overview

Connection is a read-only handle for inspecting and removing a wiring link between a source node and a target parameter in a scriptnode `DspNetwork` graph. Each Connection represents a single link from a modulation source or container macro parameter to a destination parameter.

![Scriptnode Class Hierarchy](/images/v2/scripting-api/topology_scriptnode-hierarchy.svg)

`Connection` represents a wiring link between two `Parameter` objects across different nodes in the same `DspNetwork`.

Connections are created through the source or target side of the link:

```js
// From the source node
const var cn = modNode.connectTo(targetParam, 0);

// From the target parameter
const var cn = param.addConnectionFrom(connectionData);
```

Once created, a Connection lets you:

- Query the source node and target parameter
- Check the modulation update rate (block size of the lowest common container)
- Test whether the connection is still active
- Remove the connection from the graph

::tip
Connection objects become invalid after `disconnect()` is called or the connected node is deleted. After invalidation, `isConnected()` returns false and getter methods return undefined or zero. It is safe to hold a reference to a disconnected Connection - the object uses weak references internally.
::

::common-mistakes
---
mistakes:
  - wrong: "Using `cn.getSourceNode(false)` to find the signal generator"
    right: "Use `cn.getSourceNode(true)` to trace through cable nodes"
    reason: "With `false`, the returned node may be a routing cable intermediary rather than the actual signal source. Pass `true` to trace through cable nodes to the real source."
---
::
## Usage Example

```javascript
// Connect a modulation source to a target parameter
const var cn = modNode.connectTo(targetParam, 0);

// Inspect the connection
Console.print(cn.isConnected());           // true
Console.print(cn.getUpdateRate());         // block size (e.g. 512)

var source = cn.getSourceNode(true);       // actual signal source
var target = cn.getTarget();               // target Parameter object

// Remove the connection
cn.disconnect();
Console.print(cn.isConnected());           // false
```

## Methods

::method-heading{name="disconnect"}
::

```javascript
cn.disconnect();
```

Removes this connection from the scriptnode graph. The source node's parameter chain is rebuilt automatically after removal.

::warning{title="Connection object is invalidated after removal"}
After calling `disconnect()`, the Connection object still exists in script but is no longer valid. `isConnected()` returns false and `getSourceNode()` returns undefined. Check `isConnected()` before calling getters if you hold a reference to a connection that may have been removed.
::

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "isConnected", to: "#isconnected" }
  - { label: "Node.connectTo", to: "/v2/scripting-api/node#connectto" }
  - { label: "Parameter.addConnectionFrom", to: "/v2/scripting-api/parameter#addconnectionfrom" }
---
::

---

::method-heading{name="getConnectionType"}
::

```javascript
var type = cn.getConnectionType();
```

Returns an integer indicating the connection source type: `0` for macro parameter connections, `1` for single-output modulation connections, and `2` for multi-output modulation connections.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "getSourceNode", to: "#getsourcenode" }
  - { label: "Node.connectTo", to: "/v2/scripting-api/node#connectto" }
  - { label: "Parameter.addConnectionFrom", to: "/v2/scripting-api/parameter#addconnectionfrom" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: getSourceNode
params:
  - { name: getSignalSource, type: int, desc: "If true, traces through cable nodes to the real signal source. If false, returns the immediate source node." }
---
::

```javascript
var src = cn.getSourceNode(true);
```


Returns the source node of this connection. The `getSignalSource` parameter controls whether cable intermediaries (such as `routing.local_cable` or `routing.global_cable`) are traced through to find the actual signal-producing node.

- Pass `true` to trace through cable nodes and return the real signal source.
- Pass `false` to return the immediate source node, which may be a cable routing node.

::warning{title="Returns undefined when disconnected"}
Returns undefined (not null) when the connection has been removed. Check `isConnected()` before calling this method if you need to distinguish a disconnected connection from a genuine lookup failure.
::

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "getTarget", to: "#gettarget" }
  - { label: "isConnected", to: "#isconnected" }
---
::

---

::method-heading{name="getTarget"}
::

```javascript
var param = cn.getTarget();
```

Returns the target [Parameter](/v2/scripting-api/parameter) object that this connection feeds into. Returns undefined if the target node has been deleted.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "getSourceNode", to: "#getsourcenode" }
  - { label: "isConnected", to: "#isconnected" }
  - { label: "disconnect", to: "#disconnect" }
  - { label: "Parameter.addConnectionFrom", to: "/v2/scripting-api/parameter#addconnectionfrom" }
---
::

---

::method-heading{name="getUpdateRate"}
::

```javascript
var rate = cn.getUpdateRate();
```

Returns the block size of the lowest common container ancestor of the source and target nodes. This value reflects how often the modulation value is updated - containers with smaller block sizes update more frequently. Returns 0 if the connection is disconnected or the common container could not be resolved.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "getSourceNode", to: "#getsourcenode" }
  - { label: "getTarget", to: "#gettarget" }
  - { label: "isConnected", to: "#isconnected" }
---
::

---

::method-heading{name="isConnected"}
::

```javascript
var valid = cn.isConnected();
```

Returns whether this connection is still active in the scriptnode graph. Returns false after `disconnect()` has been called or if the connected node was deleted.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "disconnect", to: "#disconnect" }
---
::

---

text: Top-level scriptnode DSP graph container for creating, connecting, and processing audio nodes.
body:
::category-tags
---
tags:
  - { name: scriptnode, desc: "ScriptNode DSP graph system" }
  - { name: container, desc: "Stores and organizes data or child elements" }
---
::

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "Node", to: "/v2/scripting-api/node", desc: "DspNetwork is the top-level graph container; Node is a single processing element inside the network." }
  - { label: "Builder", to: "/v2/scripting-api/builder", desc: "DspNetwork manages the ScriptNode DSP graph (create/connect nodes); Builder programmatically creates the HISE module tree (synths, effects, modulators) -- different systems entirely." }
---
::



## Overview

`DspNetwork` is the top-level container for a scriptnode DSP graph and the entry point for all scriptnode scripting operations. It manages a tree of processing nodes that define an audio signal chain.

![Scriptnode Class Hierarchy](/images/v2/scripting-api/topology_scriptnode-hierarchy.svg)

The following modules can host a DspNetwork:

| Processor ID | UI Name | Module Type |
|---|---|---|
| `ScriptFX` | Script FX | Master Effect |
| `PolyScriptFX` | Polyphonic Script FX | Voice Effect |
| `ScriptSynth` | Scriptnode Synthesiser | Sound Generator |
| `ScriptTimeVariantModulator` | Script Time Variant Modulator | Time Variant Modulator |
| `ScriptEnvelopeModulator` | Script Envelope Modulator | Envelope Modulator |

These modules are dual-purpose: they run plain HiseScript by default and become scriptnode hosts when `Engine.createDspNetwork()` is called inside them. Plain Script Processors and Script Voice Start Modulators cannot host a DspNetwork.

A DspNetwork provides:

1. **Visual graph authoring** - build signal chains in the scriptnode editor with immediate visual feedback, saved as XML
2. **Node lifecycle management** - create, look up, and remove nodes identified by factory path and unique ID
3. **Parameter forwarding** - expose root node parameters to DAW automation
4. **C++ compilation pipeline** - convert authored graphs to compiled C++ for production performance without changing the authoring workflow
5. **Undo support** - transaction-based undo for graph editing operations in the HISE IDE

## How to Obtain

There are several ways to create or access a DspNetwork:

| Method | Returns | When to Use |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| UI workflow (package icon / XML file selection) | - | Default approach. Sufficient for most use cases where you do not need to interact with the network from script. |
| []($API$Engine#createDspNetwork) | `DspNetwork` | When you need a script reference to the network on the same processor - e.g. programmatic node creation, parameter queries, or `setForwardControlsToParameters()`. |
| `Engine.getDspNetworkReference("processorId", "id")` | `DspNetwork` | When accessing a scriptnode network from the main interface script, avoiding complex cross-module script communication. |
| `SlotFX.setEffect("networkName")` | `Effect` | When dynamically swapping between multiple scriptnode networks at runtime via the Effect API. Does not return a DspNetwork directly. |

For most workflows, the visual approach is sufficient: create a DspNetwork in the HISE IDE using the package icon in a script processor module, build the graph in the scriptnode editor, and leave the script callbacks empty. The hosting processor handles audio routing automatically.

When you do need a script reference:

```javascript
// On the same processor
const var nw = Engine.createDspNetwork("MyNetwork");

// From the main interface script (cross-processor access)
const var nw = Engine.getDspNetworkReference("ScriptFX1", "MyNetwork");
```

For advanced use cases, nodes can be created programmatically using `create()`, `createAndAdd()`, or `createFromJSON()`. Nodes are identified by a factory path in `factory.node` format (e.g. `core.gain`, `container.split`) and a unique string ID. Bracket syntax provides shorthand node access:

```javascript
const var ref = nw["myGain"];
```

The graph architecture consists of a hierarchical tree rooted at a `container.chain` node. Node factories (container, core, math, fx, and others) create nodes by matching the factory path prefix. Root node parameters are automatically bridged to the host DAW when parameter forwarding is enabled.

::warning{title="Host modules only"}
Only the five module types listed above can host a DspNetwork. Using `Engine.createDspNetwork()` in a plain Script Processor or Script Voice Start Modulator reports an error.
::

::tip{title="No bracket assignment"}
Assignment via bracket syntax (`nw["id"] = value`) is not supported and reports a script error. Use node parameter methods instead.
::

::common-mistakes
---
mistakes:
  - wrong: "Writing custom `processBlock` logic to feed audio into a hosted network"
    right: "Leave `processBlock` empty and let the hosting processor handle audio routing"
    reason: "The hosting processor automatically connects the network to the audio stream. Manual `processBlock` is only needed for standalone buffer processing outside a hosted context."
  - wrong: "Creating nodes programmatically when the graph is static"
    right: "Use the visual scriptnode editor and save as XML"
    reason: "Programmatic creation adds complexity without benefit for fixed signal chains. The visual editor provides immediate feedback and the XML format supports compilation to C++."
---
::
## Usage Example

```javascript
// Create a DspNetwork (must be in a Scriptnode-capable processor)
const var nw = Engine.createDspNetwork("MyNetwork");

// Create nodes programmatically
const var gain = nw.create("core.gain", "myGain");
const var osc = nw.create("core.oscillator", "myOsc");

// Access a node by ID (bracket syntax)
const var ref = nw["myGain"];
```

## Methods

::method-heading
---
name: clear
params:
  - { name: removeNodesFromSignalChain, type: int, desc: "If true, removes all child nodes and parameters from the root node" }
  - { name: removeUnusedNodes, type: int, desc: "If true, deletes nodes not in any signal path" }
---
::

```javascript
nw.clear(true, true);
```


Removes nodes from the network. The two flags operate independently: `removeNodesFromSignalChain` detaches all child nodes and parameters from the root container, while `removeUnusedNodes` deletes any nodes not currently in a signal path and triggers garbage collection. Both flags accept `0` or `1`.

::warning{title="Flags are independent"}
Calling `clear(true, false)` detaches nodes from the root container but leaves them registered in the network as orphaned objects. A subsequent `clear(false, true)` is needed to remove them entirely. To fully reset the network, pass `clear(true, true)`.
::

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "create", to: "#create" }
  - { label: "deleteIfUnused", to: "#deleteifunused" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: create
params:
  - { name: path, type: String, desc: "Factory path in `factory.node` format" }
  - { name: id, type: String, desc: "Unique node identifier" }
---
::

```javascript
var node = nw.create("core.gain", "myGain");
```


Creates a node with the given factory path and ID, and returns a reference to it. The factory path uses `factory.node` format (e.g. `core.gain`, `container.split`, `math.add`). If `id` is empty, a unique name is auto-generated from the path suffix. Returns `undefined` if no registered factory matches the path.

```javascript
var gain = nw.create("core.gain", "myGain");
```

::warning{title="Existing ID returns the existing node silently"}
If a node with the given `id` already exists, the method returns the existing node and ignores the `path` parameter. Calling `create("core.gain", "myOsc")` when a `core.oscillator` named "myOsc" already exists returns the oscillator, not a gain node, with no warning.
::

#### Create Nodes

```javascript
const var nw = Engine.createDspNetwork("MyNetwork");

// Create a gain node with explicit ID
const var gain = nw.create("core.gain", "myGain");

// Existing ID returns the same node regardless of path
const var ref = nw.create("core.oscillator", "myGain"); // returns the gain, not an oscillator

// Auto-generate ID by passing empty string
const var osc = nw.create("core.oscillator", "");
```

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "createAndAdd", to: "#createandadd" }
  - { label: "createFromJSON", to: "#createfromjson" }
  - { label: "get", to: "#get" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: createAndAdd
params:
  - { name: path, type: String, desc: "Factory path in `factory.node` format" }
  - { name: id, type: String, desc: "Unique node identifier" }
  - { name: parent, type: Object, desc: "Parent container node to add the new node to" }
---
::

```javascript
var node = nw.createAndAdd("core.gain", "myGain", parentNode);
```


Creates a node and immediately adds it as the last child of the given parent container. Equivalent to calling `create(path, id)` followed by `node.setParent(parent, -1)`. If `id` is empty, a unique name is auto-generated from the path suffix.

```javascript
var node = nw.createAndAdd("core.gain", "myGain", parentContainer);
```

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "create", to: "#create" }
  - { label: "createFromJSON", to: "#createfromjson" }
  - { label: "Node.setParent", to: "/v2/scripting-api/node#setparent" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: createFromJSON
params:
  - { name: jsonData, type: var, desc: "Node tree descriptor with FactoryPath, ID, and optional Nodes array" }
  - { name: parent, type: Object, desc: "Parent container node to add the top-level node to" }
---
::

```javascript
var node = nw.createFromJSON(nodeTree, parentNode);
```


Recursively creates a tree of nodes from a JSON descriptor and adds them to the given parent container. Each object in the descriptor must have `FactoryPath` and `ID` properties. An optional `Nodes` array defines child nodes, processed recursively. Returns the top-level node, or `undefined` if creation fails.

```javascript
var tree = {
    "FactoryPath": "container.chain",
    "ID": "subChain",
    "Nodes": [
        { "FactoryPath": "core.gain", "ID": "gain1" },
        { "FactoryPath": "core.gain", "ID": "gain2" }
    ]
};

var result = nw.createFromJSON(tree, rootNode);
```

#### Create From Json

```javascript
const var nw = Engine.createDspNetwork("MyNetwork");
const var root = nw.get(nw.getId());

var tree = {
    "FactoryPath": "container.chain",
    "ID": "subChain",
    "Nodes": [
        { "FactoryPath": "core.gain", "ID": "gain1" },
        { "FactoryPath": "core.gain", "ID": "gain2" }
    ]
};

var result = nw.createFromJSON(tree, root);
```

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "create", to: "#create" }
  - { label: "createAndAdd", to: "#createandadd" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: createTest
params:
  - { name: testData, type: var, desc: "Test configuration object" }
---
::

```javascript
var test = nw.createTest({"SignalType": "Noise"});
```


Creates a `ScriptNetworkTest` object for automated testing of this network. The `testData` JSON object configures the test (e.g. signal type, processing specs). The test object provides methods for running tests, setting properties, and asserting expected values.

```javascript
var test = nw.createTest({"SignalType": "Noise"});
```

::warning{title="Backend only"}
Returns `undefined` silently in exported plugins. Guard any test code with a backend check to avoid calling methods on `undefined`.
::

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "API.ScriptNetworkTest", to: "/v2/scripting-api/api#scriptnetworktest" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: get
params:
  - { name: id, type: String, desc: "Node identifier to look up. Also accepts a Node reference (returned as-is)" }
---
::

```javascript
var node = nw.get("myGain");
```


Returns a reference to the node with the given ID. If the ID matches the network's own ID, returns the root node. Returns `undefined` if no node with the given ID exists. Also accepts a Node reference, which is returned as-is.

```javascript
var node = nw.get("myGain");
var root = nw.get(nw.getId());
```

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "create", to: "#create" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: prepareToPlay
params:
  - { name: sampleRate, type: double, desc: "Audio sample rate in Hz" }
  - { name: blockSize, type: double, desc: "Audio block size in samples" }
---
::

```javascript
nw.prepareToPlay(44100.0, 512);
```


Initialises the network for audio processing at the given sample rate and block size. Must be called before `processBlock()`. If `sampleRate` is zero or negative, the method returns without doing anything.

When hosting a DspNetwork in any of the five DspNetwork-capable modules (Script FX, Polyphonic Script FX, Scriptnode Synthesiser, Script Time Variant Modulator, Script Envelope Modulator), the hosting processor calls this automatically. Manual calls are only needed when processing buffers outside a hosted context.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "processBlock", to: "#processblock" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: processBlock
params:
  - { name: data, type: Array, desc: "Array of Buffer objects, one per audio channel" }
---
::

```javascript
nw.processBlock([ch1, ch2]);
```


Processes audio data through the network's node graph. The `data` parameter is an array of `Buffer` objects, one per channel. All buffers must have the same sample count.

When hosting a DspNetwork in any of the five DspNetwork-capable modules (Script FX, Polyphonic Script FX, Scriptnode Synthesiser, Script Time Variant Modulator, Script Envelope Modulator), the hosting processor routes audio automatically. Leave this callback empty in hosted contexts.

::warning{title="Silent no-output without initialisation"}
If the network has not been initialised via `prepareToPlay()`, processing is silently skipped. No error is thrown - the buffers are left unmodified.
::

#### Process Block Manual

```javascript
const var nw = Engine.createDspNetwork("MyNetwork");

nw.prepareToPlay(44100.0, 512);

const var ch1 = Buffer.create(512);
const var ch2 = Buffer.create(512);

// Process stereo audio through the node graph
nw.processBlock([ch1, ch2]);
```

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "prepareToPlay", to: "#preparetoplay" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: setForwardControlsToParameters
params:
  - { name: shouldForward, type: int, desc: "If true, UI controls drive network parameters directly" }
---
::

```javascript
nw.setForwardControlsToParameters(true);
```


Controls whether UI control values are forwarded directly to the network's root node parameters or routed through regular script callbacks. Enabled by default.

When forwarding is enabled, parameters defined on the root `container.chain` node are exposed to DAW automation. Disable forwarding only when you need custom script-side parameter processing logic between the UI controls and the network.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "setParameterDataFromJSON", to: "#setparameterdatafromjson" }
---
::

---

::method-heading
---
name: setParameterDataFromJSON
params:
  - { name: jsonData, type: var, desc: "Object with `nodeId.parameterId` keys and numeric values" }
---
::

```javascript
nw.setParameterDataFromJSON({"myGain.Gain": -6.0});
```


Sets multiple node parameters from a JSON object. Each property key uses `nodeId.parameterId` format, and the value is a number. Matched parameters are updated with undo support.

```javascript
nw.setParameterDataFromJSON({
    "myGain.Gain": -6.0,
    "myOsc.Frequency": 440.0,
    "myFilter.Cutoff": 2000.0
});
```

#### Set Params From Json

```javascript
const var nw = Engine.createDspNetwork("MyNetwork");

// Keys use "nodeId.parameterId" format
nw.setParameterDataFromJSON({
    "myGain.Gain": -6.0,
    "myOsc.Frequency": 440.0,
    "myFilter.Cutoff": 2000.0
});
```

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "Node.setParameterWithString", to: "/v2/scripting-api/node#setparameterwithstring" }
  - { label: "setForwardControlsToParameters", to: "#setforwardcontrolstoparameters" }
  - { label: "undo", to: "#undo" }
---
::

---

::method-heading{name="undo"}
::

```javascript
nw.undo();
```

Undoes the last action in the network's undo history. Operations are grouped into transactions every 1500ms. Returns `true` if an action was successfully undone. Undo is enabled by default in the HISE IDE but disabled in exported plugins.

::see-also
---
links:
  - { label: "setParameterDataFromJSON", to: "#setparameterdatafromjson" }
---
::

---
